title: dukecodes project template
eyebrow: DevSecOps project template · free and open
headline: Learn security by
shipping real projects.
lede: A starter kit with the same security checks big companies use, already switched on and explained in plain English. Watch the gates catch real attacks, then build it yourself step by step. No tech background needed.

stages.title: Get your copy
stages.intro: Make your own repository from this template.

steps.title: Create a repo from the template
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: A template copies every file into a fresh repository with no shared history, so your project starts clean.
steps.do: On GitHub, open this repo and press Use this template, then Create a new repository. Pick Private unless you mean to share it.
steps.check: Your new repo shows the same files and a single first commit.
steps.undo: Settings › Danger zone › Delete this repository.

steps.title: Copy it to your computer
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: You edit and test on your own machine, then send changes back. `git clone` makes that local copy.
steps.do: Replace YOUR-REPO with the name you picked.
steps.check: `git status` says `On branch main` and `nothing to commit`.
steps.undo: Delete the folder. Nothing on GitHub changes.

stages.title: Make it yours
stages.intro: Rename the starter and switch on the local checks.

steps.title: Rename the project
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: The starter code is called `app`. Renaming once now keeps names consistent everywhere.
steps.do: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
steps.check: `src/` now holds a folder named after your project and the README title changed.
steps.undo: `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd` restores the template files.
out: Renamed to my-project. Next: edit CLAUDE.md line 3 and pyproject authors, then make setup.

steps.title: Install tools and git hooks
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: Hooks run the security checks every time you commit, so a leaked password is caught on your laptop, not after it reaches GitHub.
steps.do: Needs `uv` installed (one line from astral.sh). Or open the repo in the dev container, which runs this for you.

steps.title: Run every check
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: Proves the tools work before you write anything. If this passes, CI will too.
steps.check: Every line says `Passed` and tests report `passed`.
steps.warn: If the scan step says semgrep loaded no rules, your network blocks semgrep.dev. That is a failure, not a pass.

stages.title: Ship a change safely
stages.intro: The loop you repeat for every change.

steps.title: Work on a branch
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: `main` is what everyone trusts. Branches let you experiment without breaking it. The hooks refuse commits straight to main.
steps.check: `git branch` shows a star next to `my-first-change`.

steps.title: Open a pull request and watch CI
steps.label: FACT
steps.why: A pull request (PR) runs every gate on GitHub's machines and gives you a record to show in interviews.
steps.do: Commit, push the branch, then open the PR link git prints. Fill in the template's security checklist.
steps.do_cmd:
git add -A
git commit -m "Describe the change"
git push -u origin my-first-change
steps.check: The PR shows green checks for lint, test, scan and dependency-review.
steps.undo: Close the PR. The branch can be deleted from the PR page.
out: remote: Create a pull request for 'my-first-change' on GitHub by visiting:

steps.title: Record the decision
steps.label: INFERENCE
steps.why: Interviewers ask why, not what. A short decision record (ADR) per trade-off is your answer, written while it's fresh.
steps.do: Copy `docs/adr/0000-template.md` to the next number and fill in Context, Decision, Pros, Cons.
steps.check: The ADR is in the PR and linked from its description.
steps.undo: Mark it `superseded` in a later ADR. Never delete history.

gates.name: gitleaks
gates.stops: Passwords, tokens and keys committed by mistake.

gates.name: semgrep
gates.stops: Risky code patterns (SAST): injection, unsafe calls. Fails if no rules load.

gates.name: trivy
gates.stops: Known-vulnerable dependencies, secrets in files, insecure Docker/IaC settings.

gates.name: zizmor + actionlint
gates.stops: Unsafe or broken GitHub Actions workflows.

gates.name: ruff, shellcheck, yamllint
gates.stops: Bugs and sloppy code in Python, shell scripts and YAML.

gates.name: dependency-review
gates.stops: A PR that adds a dependency with a high-severity CVE.

gates.name: Claude guardrails
gates.stops: AI helper reading secrets, force-pushing, or changing real infrastructure.

glossary.def: A project folder with its full change history, stored by git.
A saved snapshot of your changes with a message saying why.
A separate line of work. Merge it into main when it's ready.
A request to merge a branch. Where checks run and reviews happen.
Continuous integration: GitHub runs the checks on every change automatically.
A check that runs on your machine before git saves a commit.
Searching files for passwords and keys before they leak.
Static analysis: reading code for security bugs without running it.
A public ID for a known security bug, like CVE-2026-33634.
Breaking in through a tool or library you trust instead of your own code.
Referring to a tool by its exact fingerprint, so nobody can swap it under a familiar name.
A GitHub bot that proposes updates. Here it waits 7 days so bad releases get caught first.
Give each job only the access it needs, nothing more.
Architecture decision record: a one-page note on a choice and its trade-offs.
A ready-made workspace with every tool installed, so a new device works in minutes.
A fast Python tool that installs packages and locks exact versions.
A password-like string a program uses to log in. Leak it and someone else can act as you.
Tricking a program into running attacker input as code or commands.

footer: Built from `dukecodes-project-template`. Design: Mission Control tokens in `site/assets/`.

scenarios.title: Clean change
scenarios.lesson: Every gate passed, so the change can be reviewed and merged. This happens in about a minute on every push.

scenarios.title: Leaked token
scenarios.summary: An API token pasted into code by mistake.
scenarios.lesson: The token never left your laptop. If it had reached GitHub, you would have to rotate it: bots scan public repos for keys within minutes.

scenarios.title: Hijacked action tag
scenarios.summary: A workflow uses `@v4` instead of an exact SHA.
scenarios.lesson: Tags can be moved to malicious code, as happened to trivy-action in March 2026. A SHA pin always means the exact code you reviewed.

scenarios.title: Injection bug
scenarios.summary: User input passed straight into a shell command.
scenarios.finding: subprocess-shell-true: user input reaches shell=True in src/app/run.py:8
scenarios.lesson: SAST reads code for dangerous patterns before it runs. Fix: pass a list of arguments and never use `shell=True` with input.

scenarios.title: Vulnerable library
scenarios.summary: A dependency with a known critical CVE.
scenarios.lesson: Most real breaches use known bugs in old libraries. trivy compares your lock file against CVE databases on every push. (Example CVE for demo.)

features.title: Secrets never leave your laptop
features.text: Passwords and tokens are caught before they're saved, not after they leak.

features.title: Supply chain locked down
features.text: Every outside tool is pinned to an exact fingerprint. Updates wait 7 days so bad releases get caught first.

features.title: Guardrails for AI helpers
features.text: Claude Code can read and suggest, but can't read secrets, force-push, or touch real servers.

features.title: One command checks everything
features.text: `make check` runs the same gates as CI. Green locally means green on GitHub.

features.title: Any device in minutes
features.text: Open the dev container on a new laptop or in the browser. Every tool comes installed.

features.title: Interview-ready by design
features.text: Decision records and a clean PR history show why, not just what. That's what hiring managers ask about.

features.title: Learn by breaking things
features.text: The live demo lets you try real attack patterns safely and see exactly which control stops each one.

path.title: Get it running
path.text: Copy the template, run `make check`, see every gate pass.

path.title: Ship a change
path.text: Branch, commit, open a PR, watch CI. Break it on purpose once.

path.title: Build a project
path.text: Your own tool or lab on this base, with ADRs for each choice.

path.title: Show your work
path.text: Walk through your repo: the gates, the decisions, the attacks you blocked.

final.title: Your first secure project starts today.
final.text: Everything here is free. Copy the template, follow the runbook, and you'll have something real to show, and to explain, by the end of the week.
